summary: the supervisor writes <flumeDir>/run-end.json — reason, signal or exit code, time — and status reports it, naming the stale-pidfile case rather than guessing
acceptance: every supervisor end writes the record with its reason, a SIGHUP ends the run through the same teardown as SIGTERM, and status prints the recorded end or says the current run died without recording one
tests: the supervisor writes run-end.json naming hibernation as the reason it ended
a run ended by the stop flag records the stop flag as its reason
a run ended by the tick budget records the budget as its reason
a run ended by a signal records the signal
a SIGHUP ends the run through the same teardown as SIGTERM
flume status reports the reason and time run-end.json records
flume status says the current run died without recording an end beside a stale loop.pid

laneTests.title: a SIGBREAK ends the run through the same teardown as SIGTERM

notes: The handlers are installed in one place today (src/cliTeardown.ts:93-94, `exit`/SIGINT/SIGTERM) — the two new signals are rows there, not a second install site. A death no handler runs on records nothing; that case is status's to report, never the supervisor's to guess.
